transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Chen, and daughter, thank you for coming back in. I need to talk to you about your grandson's vaccinations from this morning. There was a mistake. We gave him a dose of the vaccine that was meant for an older, heavier child, not a baby his size.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I mean the amount of medicine in the needle was too high for his weight. It was the wrong dose. Does that make sense so far?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Too much? He is okay?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am sorry. This was my mistake in preparing the medicine. I apologize for this error.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why? Why you do this? He is so small, you see he is small.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. Now, the most important thing is that we have looked at the data and the risk of a severe reaction is very low.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am scared. He was crying so much and now you say this. I don't know if I can trust—

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is a very common vaccine, and I can tell you that the clinical outcome is usually fine. Do you understand that the dose was too high, or should I explain it again?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I understand too much medicine. But he is just a baby. My heart is shaking.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. But we have to look at the facts here. The dose was for a child about ten kilos heavier.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't know what kilos is. Is he going to be sick? Is he going to be—

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Look, I have to get to my next appointment in a few minutes, so let's focus on the now. He is stable.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are leaving? But we are talking about my grandson!

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I just mean we should be efficient. Like I said, it is a mistake, I am sorry it happened, and he is fine.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: He is not fine if you are rushing. I feel very bad. I feel like you just—

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. But really, the medical risk is minimal.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But what do we do? Do we go to the hospital? Do we give him medicine to stop the other medicine?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We just need to keep an eye on him.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: How? What do I look for?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Just watch him. If he seems different, let us know.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Different how? Does he get a fever? Does he stop eating? You have to tell me what to do.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will probably just see how he does over the next few days. Just stay tuned for an email from the office.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I do not check email. I told you, I do not use the computer. My daughter does. But I want to know now.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Just have your daughter watch the email. We will be in touch.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is all? An email? He had too much medicine!

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I've already apologized for the error. There isn't anything more to do clinically right now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am very confused. I don't feel right about this.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I really have to go now. We'll just keep monitoring it.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language repeatedly ('get to my next appointment', 'be efficient', 'really have to go now') and shows defensive escalation.

E.justification: Error was named explicitly in the first turn using lay language, and comprehension was checked ('Does that make sense so far?').

A.justification: Resident used direct apology language ('I am sorry', 'I apologize') and took personal responsibility ('my mistake') without deflection.

R.justification: Resident only used generic validation ('I understand') and consistently met emotional bids with factual redirection.

T.justification: The plan consists only of placeholders and vague instructions ('keep an eye on him', 'stay tuned for an email') with no specific symptoms or timelines.
